concepts.title: Unity in Diversity: Many in the One

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Unity in Diversity: Many in the One' refers to.
questions.a: India holds many languages, dresses, foods and customs within one civilisation; thinkers call this unity in diversity, or the Many in the One, the deep pattern of Indian life.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Unity in Diversity: Many in the One'.
questions.a: Difference does not divide here: the many forms share one inner culture, as Tagore and Sri Aurobindo describe.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Unity in Diversity: Many in the One', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Diversity of Languages, Dress and Food

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Diversity of Languages, Dress and Food' refers to.
questions.a: A train journey across India shows the diversity at once: landscapes change, languages and scripts shift, dresses and dishes differ from station to station, yet travellers remain at home in one country.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Diversity of Languages, Dress and Food'.
questions.a: Diversity meets you at every mile, and every mile still speaks of India.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Diversity of Languages, Dress and Food' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: A rich diversity (source: fees108.txt, A rich diversity)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Epics and Shared Stories' refers to.
questions.a: The same epics and tales, the Mahabharata and Ramayana, bhakti songs and folk retellings, travel across India in every language, joining regions that never met into one story-loving family.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Epics and Shared Stories'.
questions.a: Shared stories are shared values: when millions know the same heroes, they feel one people.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Epics and Shared Stories' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Many Expressions of Diversity' refers to.
questions.a: Diversity becomes strength when the many forms are honoured: festivals, foods, arts and faiths are different expressions of one human search, and respecting them keeps the country's fabric whole.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Many Expressions of Diversity'.
questions.a: The one appears in the many: honouring another's way of worship or dress strengthens, not weakens, the nation.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Many Expressions of Diversity' taught, and from which source text?
